title: Ops telemetry canvas: session slices and sampling
content:
Purpose

This is a working canvas for the next telemetry sprint focused on two related priorities: making tenant/session slices meaningful for investigation and bounding trace ingestion cost with a sampling budget tied to KV/cache warming signals. This doc is intentionally framing-first: why we need the signals, what we intend to measure, how traces map to dashboards, and a practical sampling configuration to balance operator visibility vs query cost.

Audience
- Observability team (primary)
- SREs and runtime engineers
- Serving and batching owners
- Solutions engineers who will interpret dashboards with customers

Goals and success criteria (MVP)
1) Define a compact signal set that lets an operator answer: "Is this latency spike tenant-local, model-cold-start, or KV-eviction related?"
   - Success metric: 80% of triages can be resolved with dashboard + 1 trace within 15 minutes (measured by a 4-week trial).
2) Produce a tenant-session slice dashboard template (microdash) that is inexpensive to query and can be pinned by solutions teams.
   - Success metric: template used by at least 3 teams in beta and average query time < 300ms.
3) Implement a sampling policy that caps trace volume for less-probable events while ensuring full capture for high-severity failure modes.
   - Success metric: trace ingestion growth <= 10% vs baseline during rollout; high-severity flows sampled at >= 95%.

Signal inventory (compact)
- request.count (per-tenant, per-route)
- request.latency.p50/p95/p99 (per-tenant, per-route)
- model.variant.kv_cache.hits / .misses (tenant-tagged)
- kv.cache.warmth_index (0..1 scalar per session)
- session.kv_prefixes_warmed (count)
- request.token_path.length (tokens)
- runtime.batch.size_distribution (quantiles)
- fallback.invocations (counts with cause tag: capacity|error|policy)
- trace.capture_reason (enum: alert|sampling_rule|manual|synthetic)

Metric definition conventions (compact canonical names and dimensions)
- Canonical name: snake.case lower with dot separators for logical groups.
- Required dimensions: tenant_id, route, model_name, model_version, region, trace_id (when available).
- Aggregation window: default 1m for operational metrics, 1h for business/usage.
- Units: seconds for latency, counts for hits/misses, ratio for warmth_index.

Key metric definitions (examples)
- request.latency.p95: 95th percentile server processing time for requests (ingress->first-token-emitted). Dimension: tenant_id, route, model_name, region.
- kv.cache.warmth_index: fraction of prefixes found in local KV cache within a session window (0..1). Computed as warmed_prefixes / total_prefixes_seen. Tag with session_id, tenant_id.
- session.kv_prefixes_warmed: incremental count of distinct prefixes warmed for a session (useful for correlating first N tokens cost).

Tracing span model and semantic conventions
- High-level spans: request.root (server handler), request.model.infer, request.kv.lookup, request.routing, request.fallback, request.batch.wait
- Important span tags/attributes:
  - tenant_id (string)
  - route (string)
  - session_id (string)
  - kv_prefix (string, optional; hash in prod to avoid PII leakage)
  - kv_hit (bool)
  - model_version (string)
  - batch_size (int)
  - tokens_generated (int)
  - capture_reason (enum)
- Span naming guidance: use short verbs and the resource e.g., "kv.lookup", "model.decode", "batch.enqueue". Keep span durations additive to allow waterfall analysis.

Sampling policy proposal (tiered)
- Background: trace volume is dominated by high-QPS, low-severity requests. We need to capture full traces for high-severity and for sessions when KV-warmth transitions happen.
- Rules (evaluated in order):
  1) Always-sample if fallback.invocation=true OR error code >= 500 OR request.latency > 3x p95 (tenant route).
  2) Session-warmth rule: if session.kv_prefixes_warmed increases by >= 5 within 60s, sample 100% of traces for that session for the next 10 minutes.
  3) Heuristic tenant sampling: for tenants with fewer than 100 req/min, sample at 25% to preserve coverage.
  4) Default reservoir: sample 1% of requests globally, with stratified reservoir by model_name to avoid starving low-volume models.
- Budgeting: start with a 10M spans/month cap. Estimate: avg spans per sampled full trace = 8. With 10M cap -> ~1.25M full traces/month. Tune after 2-week telemetry run.

Dashboard composition guidance (microdash template)
- Goal: single-pane triage for a tenant/session event. Keep to 6 widgets (fast queries):
  1) Key SLI panel: p50/p95/p99 for the tenant (last 1h, 24h rollup)
  2) KV warmth sparkline + current warmth_index (1m resolution)
  3) Session-specific prefix warming timeline (event marks where warming spike occurred)
  4) Model variant load (percent of traffic per variant)
  5) Trace-sample chooser: quick links to last captured traces (by capture_reason)
  6) Cost/throughput KPI row: tokens/s, batch size distribution quick stat
- Widget performance tips:
  - Use pre-aggregated counters where possible (1m rollups)
  - For session-scoped timelines use sampled logs or compact rollups (avoid full-event queries)
  - Flatten tenant filters into the dashboard URL so operations can pin and share per-tenant views

Investigation playbook (operator flow)
1) Look at SLI panel. Is the spike tenant-limited? If no, check region/global indicators.
2) Open KV warmth sparkline: did warmth drop before latency rose? If yes, open recent traces for that session (trace.capture_reason=\"session-warmth\").
3) If traces not available, use session.kv_prefixes_warmed and request.batch.wait distribution to infer cold-start vs batching effect.
4) If fallback.invocations increased, inspect fallback tag reasons and correlate with model_variant.load.

Instrumentation checklist for owners (runtime + serving)
- Emit session_id on every request context (UUID).
- Ensure KV lookup spans include kv_hit boolean and hashed kv_prefix attribute.
- Add capture_reason when invoking trace sampling rules from the pipeline (alert, manual, sampling_rule, synthetic).
- Export warmth_index at session close and at 30s cadence while active.
- Expose model_variant in the root span and as service tag for rollups.

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0 (1 week): implement metric emitters and trace tags in staging, no sampling rules enabled (dry run only).
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): enable sampling rules in canary region for subset tenants (internal & beta). Monitor trace ingestion and dashboard performance.
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): expand to 50% of production traffic using tiered reservoir and session-warmth rule.
- Phase 3 (ongoing): full rollout + automated alerts when budget > 80% consumed.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How to best hash/aggregate kv_prefix to allow debugging without exposing user content? Proposal: deterministic salted hash per environment, drop raw prefix in prod logs.
- Warmth_index computation: should we exclude super-short sessions (<3 tokens)? Potential bias — propose separate metric for micro-sessions.
- Trace budget: do we want dynamic scaling with cost center (chargeback)? Action: finance + eng to propose cost allocation model (linked artifact OBS-412).

Next actions (owners and short horizon)
- [Maya] Draft PR with span tag schema and example instrumentation snippets (due: 2025-02-17).
- [Diego] Add warmth_index emitters in runtime prototype branch (due: 2025-02-21).
- [Priya] Build dashboard microdash template and wire tenant filters (due: 2025-02-24).
- [Liam] Estimate trace cost implications and map to billing centers (due: 2025-02-28).

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep the "session warming" rule conservative at first — false positives will blow budget.
- Consider a short-lived synthetic probe that intentionally creates warming transitions to validate the pipeline.
- Slack threads: #obs-session-slicing, #runtime-batching.

References and helpful links
- Jira: OBS-412 (sampling budget proposal), OBS-329 (kv-metrics onboarding)
- GitHub: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry PR #88 (span naming conventions draft)
- Confluence: obs/telemetry-canvas-2025 (long-form version)

If this canvas looks reasonable I'll convert key sections into a rollout RFC and start the instrumentation PRs.
